item.title: Electric Youth: Young People, Energy Infrastructures, and Power Cuts
item.dc:title: Electric Youth: Young People, Energy Infrastructures, and Power Cuts
item.dc:creator: John Horton Peter Kraftl José Antonio Perrella Balestieri Arminda Eugenia Marques Campos Benjamin Coles Maurício César Delamaro Rubens Alves Dias Sophie Hadfield-Hill Joseph Hall Rachel Nunes Leal Paulo Valladares Soares Catherine Walker Cristiana Zara a Faculty of Health, Life Sciences & Education, University of Northampton, UKb Department of Geography and Environment, Loughborough University, UKc School of Geography, Earth and Environmental Sciences, University of Birmingham, UKd Department of Chemistry and Energy, Sao Paulo State University, Brazile Production Engineering Department, Sao Paulo State University, Brazilf Department of Geography & Environmental Science, University of Reading, UKg School of Geography, Geology and the Environment, University of Leicester, UKh Electrical Engineering Department, Sao Paulo State University, Brazili School of Law, Education and Society, University of Hertfordshire, UKj Civil Engineering Department, Sao Paulo State University, Brazilk Department of Geography, Newcastle University, UKJOHN HORTON is Professor in the Faculty of Health, Life Sciences & Education at the University of Northampton, Northampton NN1 5PH, UK. E-mail: john.horton@northampton.ac.uk. His research explores everyday geographies, cultures, politics, playful practices, and social-material exclusions of contemporary childhood and youth.PETER KRAFTL is Professor in the Department of Geography and Environment at Loughborough University, Loughborough LE11 3TU, UK. E-mail: P.Kraftl@lboro.ac.uk. He is best known for research on children’s geographies and interdisciplinary childhood studies. His work focuses on children and young people’s experiences of and interactions with environmental processes. He also publishes on geographies of education and architecture.JOSÉ ANTONIO PERRELLA BALESTIERI is Professor in the Department of Chemistry and Energy at São Paulo State University, São Paulo 12516-410, Brazil. E-mail: jose.perrella@unesp.br. His research interests include advanced thermal cycles, wastes valorization, the water–energy–food nexus, carbon taxation, and energy modeling.ARMINDA EUGENIA MARQUES CAMPOS is Professor in the Production Engineering Department at São Paulo State University, São Paulo 12516-410, Brazil. E-mail: arminda.campos@unesp.br. Her research interests include production engineering, engineering education, tourism and sustainability, and the water–energy–food nexus.BENJAMIN COLES is Lecturer in the Department of Geography & Environmental Science at the University of Reading, RG6 6UR, UK. E-mail: b.b.coles@reading.ac.uk. His interdisciplinary research explores links between environmental impacts of commodities, markets, and their relationships to social-biodiversity and the bio-economy in the Global South, particularly in Brazil and Latin America.MAURÍCIO CÉSAR DELAMARO is Assistant Professor in the Production Engineering Department at São Paulo State University, São Paulo 12516-410, Brazil. E-mail: mauricio.delamaro@unesp.br. His research interests include product design, sustainable tourism, and the water–energy–food nexus.RUBENS ALVES DIAS is Assistant Professor in the Electrical Engineering Department at São Paulo State University, São Paulo 12516-410, Brazil. E-mail: rubens.alves@unesp.br. His research interests include electrical and mechanical engineering with a strong focus on energy systems, energy planning and policy, and engineering education.SOPHIE HADFIELD-HILL is Professor in the School of Geography, Earth and Environmental Sciences at the University of Birmingham, Birmingham B15 2TT, UK. E-mail: s.a.hadfield-hill@bham.ac.uk. Her expertise is children and young people’s everyday experiences of urban change in diverse contexts, including research in the United Kingdom, India, and Brazil.JOSEPH HALL is Lecturer in the School of Law, Education and Society at the University of Hertfordshire, Hatfield AL10 9AB, UK. E-mail: j.hall20@herts.ac.uk. His research interests include gender, LGBT+-inclusive education, and children and young people’s everyday geographies.RACHEL NUNES LEAL teaches within the São Paulo State Department of Education full-time education program, and previously held a postdoctoral fellowship in the Department of Chemistry and Energy at São Paulo State University (UNESP), 12516-410, Brazil. Email: rnunesleal@gmail.com. Her research interests include water quality, ecosystem ecology, and the water–energy–food nexus.PAULO VALLADARES SOARES is Assistant Professor in the Civil Engineering Department, at São Paulo State University, São Paulo 12516-410, Brazil. E-mail: paulo.valladares@unesp.br. He has expertise in geosciences, environmental geology, environmental education, and environmental planning, with a particular focus on the Paraíba Valley in southeastern Brazil.CATHERINE WALKER is a Postdoctoral academic track Fellow in the Department of Geography at Newcastle University, Newcastle upon Tyne NE1 7RU, UK. E-mail: Catherine.Walker@newcastle.ac.uk. Her research interests include young people’s roles in sustainability and climate adaptation agendas, progressing intergenerational and socially inclusive responses to climate change, and nexus approaches to mapping, mitigating, and conceptualizing resource insecurities with a focus on Brazil and India.CRISTIANA ZARA is a social and cultural geographer with a background in Indian studies who worked as Postdoctoral Researcher in the School of Geography, Earth and Environmental Sciences at the University of Birmingham, B15 2TT, UK. Email: c.zara@bham.ac.uk. Cristiana’s research interests include socio-economic and cultural processes of urban change and sustainability, socio-spatial justice, and everyday material and embodied geographies, with a particular focus on critical geographies of food.
